name: Neuroendocrine Neoplasm of the Pancreas

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: WHO Classification of Pancreatic Neuroendocrine Neoplasms

criteria.description: Histological confirmation of neuroendocrine tumor cells with immunohistochemical staining positive for chromogranin A and synaptophysin
Radiological evidence of pancreatic mass on CT, MRI, or somatostatin receptor scintigraphy
Elevated serum markers such as chromogranin A and specific hormone levels depending on functional status

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation plus radiological evidence of pancreatic mass
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Functional tumors may require additional hormone assays for diagnosis.

pathognomonic.notes: Occurs in functional tumors secreting insulin or other hormones
searchTerms: low blood sugar from insulin tumor

common.symptomName: Abdominal pain localized to the upper abdomen
common.notes: Due to tumor mass effect or local invasion

common.symptomName: Diarrhea associated with hormone secretion (e.g., VIPoma)
common.notes: Seen in functional tumors secreting vasoactive intestinal peptide

common.symptomName: Jaundice due to bile duct obstruction
common.notes: May occur if tumor compresses biliary tree
searchTerms: yellow skin due to bile obstruction

occasional.symptomName: Flushing episodes related to hormone secretion
occasional.notes: Seen in functional tumors such as carcinoid syndrome
Due to mass effect or hormone secretion

rare.notes: Rare electrolyte disturbance from hormone secretion

rare.symptomName: Cushingoid features due to ectopic ACTH secretion
searchTerms: symptoms of high cortisol due to ectopic hormone
signs of cortisol excess from tumor hormone

laboratory: Hormone assays depending on tumor type (insulin, gastrin, VIP, glucagon)
imaging: Contrast-enhanced CT or MRI showing pancreatic mass
Endoscopic ultrasound with fine needle aspiration
genetic: MEN1 gene mutations in familial cases
DAXX and ATRX mutations in sporadic tumors
other: Histopathological grading based on mitotic count and Ki-67 index
Immunohistochemical staining positive for synaptophysin and chromogranin A

redFlags: Unexplained severe abdominal pain with weight loss
references: WHO Classification of Tumours Editorial Board. WHO Classification of Tumours, 5th Edition, Volume 1: Digestive System Tumours. IARC; 2019.
Modlin IM, Oberg K, Chung DC, et al. Gastroenteropancreatic neuroendocrine tumours. Lancet Oncol. 2008;9(1):61-72.
Halfdanarson TR, Rabe KG, Rubin J, Petersen GM. Pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors (PNETs): incidence, prognosis and recent trend toward improved survival. Ann Oncol. 2008;19(10):1727-33.
